BLOCKED on rights (batch_030, 2026-09-04). Valued Living Questionnaire (Wilson & Groom 2002). The source study (Esiason et al. 2024, PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0300777, CC BY 4.0) publishes NO VLQ wording: it names the instrument and reports alphas only, and its S1/S2 supplements are bare REDCap xlsx exports (row 1 an export title, row 2 bare variable codes, zero embedded labels across all 194 columns). So wording could only come from the instrument itself, whose footer prints on both pages: 'Copyright (c) 2002, by Kelly Wilson. You may reproduce and use this form at will for the purpose of treatment and research. You may not distribute it without the express written consent of the author.' That is a quotable rights-holder redistribution bar, firing the 2026-09-04 no-redistribution ruling (DSES/Fetzer), which overrides the openly licensed source deposit. The ACBS-hosted 2010 Psychological Record appendix reprints the same form under the same rights holder, so it is not an independent route around the clause. RETRY TEST: NO -- determinate verdict, every source was retrieved successfully. WOULD HAVE TO CHANGE: express written consent from Kelly Wilson (kwilson@olemiss.edu), or a Ben ruling that the no-redistribution rule does not reach the VLQ. CLASS-WIDE: the identical footer governs both VLQ halves and any future VLQ table -- worth one ruling, not per-table calls. Two agents reached this block independently on the same clause. MAPPING GROUND TRUTH CAPTURED so an unblock needs no rework: codes are the source spreadsheet column names verbatim (data/esiason_2024_nmosd.py melts by name, not positionally), mapping one-to-one with VLQ domains 1-10; resp 1-10. Part 1 (importance rating): 10 items cit1 edu1 fam1 fri1 marr1 par1 phys1 rec1 spi1 wor1, 546 rows.
